title: World War II work at Higgins and USO shows
summary: Brother Tom a Marine; Jeff built boats at Higgins while doing 285 USO shows a year; Jackie Blaine singer.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: the Marines, but he was in the Marines, and he was a drill sergeant at Parris Island. He was also lightweight boxing champion of the United States Marine Corps in World War I. I was too young for World War I, and when World War II came, I was already married, and we had a child, and so I worked five years in a war plant at Higgins.

Yeah, building log torpedo boats and landing boats, and we did an average of 285 USO shows a year, besides the 10 hours a day that I worked, sometimes seven days a week, building torpedo boats. I worked my pants off in my life, thank God. I'm not ashamed of it either. Who were these USO?
I'm sorry, go ahead. I just want to ask you about the USO shows. I didn't know you did.

Well, we went all the way over to Mobile, went to Pensacola, and different bases, you know, and we were transported over there, and sometimes didn't get back until time to punch the clock in and work the next day.
And you had a band or singers too?

Steve Massico and Al Moore, that same band that I was telling you about. All of us worked in the war plant in Higgins, and they would let us all out, and we wouldn't lose any time at Higgins. And we got paid just enough compensation to pay for our food that we ate on the road. We didn't get any money for it tomorrow.
We didn't have a girl singer? No.
No. But we had one in Sharky's band, Jackie Blaine. And what became of her, I do not know.
She's almost forgotten. I don't think she made many records.
No. I don't have the slightest idea what came of her.
